note: ALEF original 10-week adult reading track. Not clergy or educator reviewed. Not derived from any book text; shape (a few letters and vowels a week, letters to words to sentences, siddur focus) follows only public course descriptions (docs/curriculum/class-track/SOURCES.md). Hebrew comes from the corpus registry by id only.

teacherPlan.what: New letters and signs: show, say, echo
Decode drill: syllables, then words, in chorus then singly

teacherSay: Move your finger from the right.
Say the name, then the sound.
Slow is fine. Read it again.
Which sign is under that letter?

weeks.title: First letters and the first word
goals: Name and sound Shin, Bet and Tav
Read the two "ah" vowels and the dot in Bet
Read the word Shabbat right to left
Hear a blessing sung or read by the teacher, no reading yet

steps.text: Point at the right edge of a line and move a finger left. Say "right to left" aloud three times.
Trace Shin and Bet in the air, then on paper. Say each name and sound.
Sound out one two-letter syllable at a time, then glue them together.

canYou: say the names and sounds of Shin, Bet and Tav
tell Bet from Vet by the dot in it
read Shabbat slowly, right to left
weeks.culture: The greeting Shabbat shalom is the first thing many people read in Hebrew.

weeks.title: Lamed, Vav, Yod and the word shalom
goals: Name and sound Lamed, final Mem, Vav and Yod
Read cholam and chirik
Read Shabbat shalom unaided
Spot the final-Mem shape
Listen for the first words of the Priestly Blessing

steps.text: Flash the six letters from last week and this week; say name, then sound.
Read the Shabbat shalom words from last week without help.
Pairs drill: a final Mem next to a regular Mem, say which is which.

canYou: read Shabbat shalom without peeking
name the vowel under a letter: kamatz, patach, cholam or chirik
say which Mem is the final one
weeks.culture: Shalom is both hello and goodbye, and it means peace.

weeks.title: Alef, He, Resh, Mem and the "ay" sound
goals: Name and sound Alef, He, Resh and Mem
Read tzere
Know that Alef carries a vowel but no sound of its own
Read short real words from the lesson lists

steps.text: Flash all letters so far, then flash all vowels so far.
Echo reading: the teacher says a short word, the class says it back, then reads it from the board.
Each person reads one syllable from the board aloud.

canYou: tell Resh from Dalet and Vav by shape
say a word that starts with Alef without adding an extra consonant
read a word with tzere
weeks.culture: Hebrew is written without capital letters; there is one shape per letter, plus five final shapes.

weeks.title: Kaf, Nun and the "oo" and "eh" vowels
goals: Name and sound Kaf (and final Kaf) and Nun (and final Nun)
Read segol, shuruk and kubutz
Hear a silent shva at the end of a word
Read the first whole line of a prayer

steps.text: Vowel round: show each vowel, the class says the sound together.
Look-alike drill: Bet or Kaf, Dalet or Resh, Vav or final Nun.
Read two words chosen from last week lessons.

canYou: tell Bet from Kaf and final Nun from Vav
read a word with shuruk and a word with kubutz
read the first line of the zimun slowly
weeks.culture: The zimun is the call that opens the blessing after a meal.

weeks.title: Shva, Pe, Chet and the Name
goals: Read a shva that starts a syllable
Name and sound Pe (and final Pe) and Chet
Meet the sneaky patach
Read the first line of the Priestly Blessing and see how the Name is written

steps.text: Flash look-alike letters, then vowels.
Syllable chips: build a two-syllable word from chips and read it.
Read last week zimun line again, faster.

canYou: read a word that starts with shva
say Chet with a scrape, not a plain h
read the first line of the Priestly Blessing
weeks.culture: The four-letter Name is not pronounced as written; readers say Adonai instead.

weeks.title: Dalet, Gimel, Ayin, Samekh, Sin and half vowels
goals: Name and sound Dalet, Gimel, Ayin, Samekh and Sin
Read the three chataf vowels
Tell Shin from Sin by the dot
Read three short prayer lines

steps.text: Letter flash with a timer on the board, no pressure.
Dot tiles: move the dot, hear the change.
Read a line from last week twice in a row.

canYou: tell Shin from Sin by the dot
read a chataf vowel as a short sound
read one of the three lines from the read-aloud list
weeks.culture: Oseh shalom closes both the standing prayer and the mourner Kaddish.

weeks.title: The alphabet is finished: Zayin, Tet, Tsadi, Qof
goals: Name and sound Zayin, Tet, Tsadi (and final) and Qof
Recognise all 27 letter shapes
Read the first line of the Shema
Read a morning line and a verse of welcome

steps.text: Alphabet song or order recited together, then individually.
Look-alike check on the new letters.
Read two lines from last week.

canYou: recognise every letter in the alphabet
read Shema line 1 slowly
tell Tet from Tav and Qof from Kaf
weeks.culture: Modeh ani is the first thing many people say on waking.

weeks.title: The full Priestly Blessing and the blessing formula
goals: Read each of the three Priestly Blessing lines
Read all three straight through
Read the common start of a blessing
Read the bread blessing

steps.text: Fast review of vowels and the Name.
Line-by-line choral reading of the three blessing lines, then in pairs.
Everyone reads the first words of a blessing.

canYou: read the three Priestly Blessing lines in order
read the start of a blessing without stopping
read the bread blessing slowly
weeks.culture: The Priestly Blessing is traditionally sung or said over children on Friday night in many homes.

weeks.title: Shva, dagesh and stress rules; the Shema
goals: Decide if a shva sounds or is silent
Tell a hard dagesh from a soft letter
Know where the stress falls
Read both lines of the Shema

steps.text: Shva quiz: show a word, class says "sounds" or "silent".
Tap out the beats of a line, then read it.
Read two blessings from last week.

canYou: say when a shva is silent
read the first Shema line without stopping
say which syllable is stressed in a word of your choice
weeks.culture: The Shema is said every morning and every evening.

weeks.title: A Friday-night page and a new page
goals: Read the Torah blessings
Read the Friday-night wine blessing
Read a line you have never seen with no help
Plan what to practise next

steps.text: Read the first line of a prayer you know by heart.
Cold read without a timer: each person reads one unseen line aloud.
Read the whole week 8 blessing together.

canYou: read a blessing you have not seen before
read at your own pace without fear of mistakes
name the next prayer you want to learn
weeks.culture: The wine blessing opens Friday-night Kiddush; the candle blessing is said at home as Shabbat begins.
